answer: One concrete defence is to charge each identity a refundable stake tied to verified work: an agent must post a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. A sybil swarm can flood one inlet with fresh accounts, but each copy must pay again, so the attack's cost grows with every clone. Genuine agents earn standing slowly, like water carving a canyon, while a mesa of new, unproven accounts stands out and can be discounted until it proves useful service.
